topic.title: Pay in 4, no interest: so who pays for it?

title: Pay in four, zero interest. So who pays for it? 🛍️
description:
Four payments, no interest: so who pays for it?
In one quarter of 2025, shops paid Affirm $239.5M on $10.4B of spending; on longer plans, buyers pay interest.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Did you think pay-later was free? Comment

lines.text: You think pay in four is free? Watch who pays.
Zero interest? Then who pays for it? The app?
The shop does. In one quarter last year, shops paid Affirm $239.5M.
That money came from all the shopping people did with Affirm.
The shop pays? How much? Per dollar?
On average, about 2.3% of every dollar spent. Paid by the shop, not the buyer.
So on zero interest, the shop pays. On longer plans, buyers pay interest too.
Still think pay in four is free money?

Re-review after rewrite. fact1 $239.5M merchant network revenue and fact2 $10.4B GMV confirmed for Affirm fiscal Q4 2025 (quarter to 30 Jun 2025): the nasdaq page returned 503 and the Affirm investor letter 403, so confirmed by search (Zacks/finanzen.net, TipRanks, FY2025 10-K on sec.gov). The figures are now dated ('one quarter last year', 'of 2025'), and the 2.3% average still matches the latest data (FY2026 10-K: merchant network revenue 2.3% of GMV), so the dated quarter is acceptable; research should still refresh the feed to fiscal Q4 2026 (about $14.1B GMV, about $302.4M merchant revenue). The framing is fixed: the question is now who pays for 0% plans, and the payoff says buyers pay interest on longer plans. Both verify items hold. No advice, the tone is fine, and the description ends with the disclaimer. Small notes: the Payoff card puts $239.5M under 'Zero interest: the shop pays', but that revenue also includes merchant fees on interest-bearing loans; some longer Affirm plans are also 0% APR, so 'often' would be more precise than 'buyers pay interest too'.

Facts fact1 ($239.5M merchant network revenue) and fact2 ($10.4B GMV) are confirmed for Affirm fiscal Q4 2025 (quarter to 30 Jun 2025) - nasdaq.com page returned 503 and the investors.affirm.com letter returned 403, confirmed by search via Zacks/finanzen.net, TipRanks and the FY2025 10-K on sec.gov - but they are out of date: four newer quarters have been reported, latest fiscal Q4 2026 (quarter to 30 Jun 2026, reported Aug 2026): GMV about $14.1B, merchant network revenue about $302.4M (Affirm FQ4'26 shareholder letter, CrowdFund Insider, FY2026 10-K: merchant network revenue 2.3% of GMV). 'In one quarter' with a 15-month-old quarter is superseded data. Research should refresh the feed facts to the latest quarter from Affirm's release/10-K.

Framing misleads (rule 3): beat 'ask' asks 'how does Affirm make money?' and beat 'shop' answers 'The shop pays it', with the payoff saying the shop pays the app. In that same quarter interest income (about $419.1M, mostly paid by buyers on interest-bearing plans) was larger than merchant network revenue ($239.5M) out of $876M total revenue, so the shop is not the main answer to how Affirm makes money. Either narrow the question to who pays for the 0% pay-in-4 plan, or say that shop fees are about a quarter of revenue and buyers paying interest on longer plans bring in more. The 'turn' line 'about 2.3% of every dollar spent' is a blended average over all GMV, including interest-bearing loans, so it is fine as an average but should not be called the fee on a 0% plan.
